claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC HEA nanoscale multilayers under sustained loading is governed by an interface-controlled mechanism.
Severe lattice distortion promotes heterogeneous dislocation nucleation and accumulation at layer interfaces.
Short-range order promotes heterogeneous dislocation nucleation and accumulation at layer interfaces.
Interface-localized dislocation nucleation and accumulation accelerate creep relative to conventional metallic multilayers.
The proposed coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC HEA layers.
The FCC/BCC HEA multilayer inherently exhibits severe lattice distortion and short-range order.
Elevated temperature can activate dislocation-mediated deformation during sustained loading.
Dislocation pile-ups, slip transmission, and local plastic instabilities are expected at the interfaces between FCC and BCC layers.
Severe lattice distortion and short-range order create a non-uniform energy landscape under sustained loading.
The non-uniform energy landscape favors dislocation nucleation and accumulation at relatively incoherent interfaces.
Diffusion-assisted dislocation climb enhances localized plasticity.
HEA multilayers will exhibit an earlier onset and faster progression of plastic deformation than conventional metallic multilayers.
HEA multilayers will develop higher dislocation densities concentrated at interfaces than conventional metallic multilayers.
HEA multilayers will exhibit increased local plastic strain concentrated at interfaces.
Sharper, more coherent interfaces will delay creep-related effects relative to chemically or structurally diffuse interfaces.
Conventional metallic multilayers typically have lower rates of interface-mediated dislocation activity under comparable creep conditions.
Conventional metallic multilayers typically exhibit more uniform dislocation glide in the bulk.
The proposed mechanism applies when temperature and stress permit diffusional processes and dislocation climb while the individual nanoscale layers remain intact.
